Signs with the fixture operator key. expires an integer of 4001 digits (under the int parse limit): math.isfinite raises OverflowError inside verify.

Signs with the fixture operator key. approver_id appears twice, first a list and then the real string. json.loads keeps the last, the signature covers it; a parser that keeps the first would see a list.
Signs with the fixture operator key. Key 'approval' twice, first null then a valid-looking token; json.loads keeps the last.
Signs with the fixture operator key. Valid-looking token for b followed by newlines to 12000 characters: the token parses and the note (2 bytes per newline) must be cut in the same dispatch.
Signs with the fixture operator key. Token for a padded with spaces and a few newlines to 11990+10 chars; note stays near the cap edge.
Note of quotes sized to land the encoded summary at the cap or one under. It fits, so nothing is cut; checks the cap is inclusive.
One more quote than the exact-fit note, so the encoded summary is at or one over the cap: the smallest oversize case.
ASCII fill that leaves 11 bytes, then emoji of 12 bytes each: the longest fitting prefix must stop before the first emoji.
ASCII fill that leaves exactly 12 bytes, then emoji: exactly one emoji fits and the rest must be cut.
ASCII fill leaving 5 bytes then e-acute (6 bytes each escaped): none fit, so the boundary falls just before the first escape.
3000 high-then-low surrogate halves as separate characters (summary_note keeps them in memory): 12 bytes per pair, oversized, tests the cut and the escape.
Low-then-high surrogate halves, the reverse order, so no pair can be joined; escapes at 6 bytes each.
12000 lone surrogates in a file channel. They are written with surrogatepass and read back as replacement characters, so the read text is longer than what was written; the note is cut to 12000.
Interleaved lone surrogates in MEMORY.md: readback turns each into replacement characters, which changes the note size from what the text length suggests.
Half-pairs ahead of JSON in a tool result: the file read grows past the relay cap of 16384 characters, so the parser is skipped by length rather than by content.
Valid JSON followed by lone surrogates: bytes are replaced on read, so trailing garbage appears and json.loads must reject it without raising.
Byte order mark in front of JSON: json.loads rejects a BOM; the relay reader must treat it as no token.
A single NUL as a tool result: fixture write and read of a NUL byte, then json.loads.
Odd line separators: carriage returns and unicode separators written as bytes and read back; no newline translation should occur.
A 4300 digit integer as the whole tool result: json.loads parses it at the int limit and the result is not a dict.
12000 open brackets: RecursionError inside json.loads in the relay reader.
Objects nested nine hundred deep under the key approval: after the recursion limit, the parse may succeed and the token reader gets a dict inside a dict.
Nested payload objects 250 deep, each with a signature: the parsed value is a dict whose payload is a dict, but without the approval fields.
12000 NUL characters in the summary note (kept in memory): 6 bytes each once escaped, so the cut must land inside a run of identical escapes.
12000 real astral characters written as 4-byte UTF-8 to MEMORY.md and read back: 12 escaped bytes each, so the repaired note is cut to a short prefix.
Noncharacters and the last code points, ending in a lone low surrogate: write as surrogatepass, read with replacement, then escape for the size test.
Eleven thousand spaces then a digit: valid JSON that is a number; the escaped note is long (spaces are one byte each) but under the cap.
Empty approval object: set(token) differs from the two required keys, so approval_schema; the cheapest dict that reaches verify.
